tools.description: Saves a new version of a project (a checkpoint on the Undo timeline). files = { path: BASE64 of the file content } — base64 is REQUIRED (the storage wire is binary-safe). By default (mode 'merge') send ONLY the files you changed: they are laid over the latest version, and paths in delete are removed. mode 'replace' = files is the whole site. label = a HUMAN sentence like 'Added the beach photos' — grandma reads this list. Idempotent. Returns { checkpoint, created, speak }.
tools.name: add_or_edit_files

tools.description: The answer to "put it on my own name": connects a domain the user owns (or just bought) to this project's site. Accepts a Domains-issued bundle confirm_token + bundle_actions so buy+connect = the SAME single yes; otherwise returns confirm_required to relay. PURE relay of the ecosystem CONFIRM_FLOW.
tools.name: connect_domain

tools.description: The answer to "make me a scrapbook / a page for my shop". Starts a new project (a private draft website). Returns { project, speak, state_proof, next_actions }.
tools.name: create_project

tools.description: Change ONE annotated part of the page ("make the headline say…"): keyed, escaped replacement saved as a new checkpoint (auto-labelled, undoable). For anything bigger use add_or_edit_files.
tools.name: edit_text

tools.description: File a project in the person's Windy Code cabinet when you START making, building or setting up something that has its own home elsewhere: a code repo, a mobile app, a database. NOT for answers or research, and NOT for websites/apps built in Windy Code (those are filed for you). Safe to repeat: the same `ref` (your own stable key, e.g. the repo URL) finds the same drawer, even if another of the person's helpers filed it. Returns { project_id, created, speak }.
tools.name: file_project

tools.description: The full knob list of the builder with trust tiers — how a new agent learns what it can do here. Also at /.well-known/windy-capabilities.json.
tools.name: get_capabilities

tools.description: Any promotions running right now (sales, free-domain offers). Mention one ONLY when it genuinely helps what the user is doing — never interrupt with it.
tools.name: get_current_promos

tools.description: The drawers in the person's cabinet that THIS helper filed or built (plus the same person's drawers it last touched), so you remember project ids across turns. Returns { drawers: [{ id, name, kind, group, summary, state, home, made_by, last_activity_at, links, waiting_for_owner }], speak }.
tools.name: list_cabinet

tools.description: The Undo timeline for a project — every saved version with its human label. Returns { checkpoints, speak }.
tools.name: list_checkpoints

tools.description: The parts of the page grandma can change directly (annotated text/images with their current values). Un-annotated content needs add_or_edit_files instead.
tools.name: list_editables

tools.description: The answer to "what am I building?" / "read me my projects". Returns { projects: [{id, name, kind, state, speak}], speak }.
tools.name: list_projects

tools.description: The six finished examples grandma can start from (scrapbook, pamphlet, personal site, event page, recipe book, business card). Offer these when she isn't sure what she wants.
tools.name: list_templates

tools.description: After a meaningful step on a filed project, add ONE plain sentence for the owner: what changed and why ('Added a search box to the recipe list.'). Never secrets, never file contents. It is always recorded as a note; the builder writes saved/published itself. Pass `idempotency_key` so a retry doesn't double it. Returns { speak }.
tools.name: log_activity

tools.description: A private tokened link to see the WORKING version before it's public (15-minute life). Use to tell the user 'here's how it looks so far'.
tools.name: preview_project

tools.description: The answer to "is my site up, and where?". Returns { project_id, name, state, url, speak, state_proof }.
tools.name: project_status

tools.description: Puts the project online. ALWAYS returns confirm_required first for agents: RELAY the question VERBATIM, then call again with the confirm_token after the human says yes. Publishing is explicit.
tools.name: publish_project

tools.description: The voice-first gallery (B3.7): everything the user has, composed to be SPOKEN — count first, then each project's name, state, and address in listening order. Use for 'read me my projects' over windy-talk.
tools.name: read_projects_aloud

tools.description: Windy Doctor for the builder — use FIRST when something seems wrong. Returns { checks: [{status, severity, finding, remediation}] } where remediation is a LITERAL next step. SAFE TO RUN.
tools.name: run_diagnostics

tools.description: Start a NEW project from what the person asked for in plain words ('a page for my bakery'): picks the closest finished example and puts your first words (fills: headline, intro, …) into the first version, so the first preview already shows them. Returns { project, template, filled, skipped_fills, editables, speak }.

fills.description: Optional first words, {edit_id: text}, e.g. headline, intro.

tools.name: start_from_prompt

tools.description: "Make mine like this": clones a finished example into a NEW project and returns the interview deck — ≤5 warm questions to ask ONE AT A TIME, then personalize with add_or_edit_files. Returns { project, interview, speak }.

fills.description: Optional first words, {edit_id: text}, e.g. headline, intro.

name.description: Her name for it (defaults to the example's title).

tools.name: start_from_template

tools.description: The giant Undo: puts an EARLIER saved version back as the working version. Reversible; does not change what's published. Returns { speak }.
tools.name: undo_to_checkpoint

tools.description: Makes a live site PRIVATE again (visitors stop seeing it; nothing is deleted). Returns confirm_required first — relay the question verbatim, then call again with the confirm_token after the human says yes.
tools.name: unpublish_project
